chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Madainy, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Two rivers are Believers, and two rivers are Infidels. So as for the two Believers, the Euphrates and the Nile of Egypt, and as for the two Infidels, the Tigris and the river of Balkh.
ai.seo_question: Which rivers are considered believers and which are considered infidels in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) classifies four major rivers into spiritual categories, attributing the status of 'believers' to the Euphrates and the Nile of Egypt, while designating the Tigris and the river of Balkh as 'infidels.' This classification reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing natural entities as possessing spiritual agency and moral alignment, often linked to their historical roles in Islamic events or their geographical proximity to key religious centers. The distinction highlights a metaphysical perspective where physical geography is intertwined with divine favor and spiritual destiny.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Ibrahim Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Two rivers are Believers, and two rivers are Infidels. So as for the two Believers, the Euphrates and Nile of Egypt, and as for the two Infidels, the Tigris and the river Balkh’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Mada’iniy who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
There are two unbelieving canals and two believing ones. The two believing canals are Euphrates and Nile of Misr (Egypt) and the unbelieving canals are Tigris and the canal of Balkh.’”
